# Quantum-group symmetry of the imaginary-coupling theories {#sec-qg-symmetry}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Construct the non-local conserved charges of imaginary-coupling affine Toda theory.
- See why they act on multi-soliton states through a non-cocommutative coproduct, and generate $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$.
- Fix the spectral parameter of the soliton multiplets from the Lorentz spins of the charges.
- Conclude that soliton S-matrices are R-matrices times scalar factors, and know what this does and does not determine.
:::

The local charges of @sec-conserved-charges make the S-matrix factorize, but they act on the solitons of a multiplet by the same number and do not distinguish them. What fixes the matrix structure of soliton scattering is a second, **non-local** symmetry. In sine-Gordon theory it was found by Bernard and LeClair [-@bernard1991], who showed that the charges generate the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ at zero centre. For a general affine Toda theory based on $\hat g$, the non-local charges generate $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$, the quantum affine algebra of the *dual* algebra [@bernard1991; @felder1992]. This chapter explains how the charges arise, why they combine into a quantum group rather than a Lie group, and what follows for the S-matrix.

## Non-local charges {#sec-nonlocal-charges}

Consider first sine-Gordon theory in the variables of @sec-sg-dictionary. At the conformal point $m_0=0$ the field splits into left- and right-moving parts, $\phi=\phi_L(x^+)+\phi_R(x^-)$, with $x^\pm=t\pm x$. Chiral vertex operators $e^{ia\phi_L}$ are holomorphic currents of conformal weight $h=a^2/8\pi$ in the normalization in which $e^{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi}$ has weights $h=\bar h=\beta_{\rm SG}^2/8\pi$.

Bernard and LeClair choose the exponent $a=8\pi/\beta_{\rm SG}$, for which $J_\pm$ has a double pole with $e^{\mp i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi}$, so that it remains conserved when the perturbation is switched on. The current carries topological charge $\pm2$, since it shifts $\phi$ by $\pm4\pi/\beta_{\rm SG}$: $[T,Q_\pm]=\pm2Q_\pm$ with $T=\pm1$ on the soliton and antisoliton.

$$
J_\pm=e^{\pm ia\phi_L},\qquad h_J=\frac{8\pi}{\beta_{\rm SG}^2}.
$$

At the conformal point $\partial_-J_\pm=0$, and $\int dx\,J_\pm$ is conserved. When the perturbation $\frac{m_0^2}{\beta_{\rm SG}^2}\cos\beta_{\rm SG}\phi$ is switched on, conformal perturbation theory shows that conservation survives to first order, and in fact exactly, in the form

$$
\partial_-J_\pm=\partial_+H_\pm ,
$$

where $H_\pm$ is proportional to $m_0^2$ times a vertex operator containing both chiralities. The conserved charges

$$
Q_\pm=\int dx\,\big(J_\pm+H_\pm\big),\qquad\bar Q_\pm=\int dx\,\big(\bar J_\pm+\bar H_\pm\big)
$$

are built from right-movers in the second case. They are **non-local**, because $\phi_L$ is a non-local functional of $\phi$ and its conjugate momentum: $\phi_L(x)$ involves $\int^x\pi\,dy$. Their Lorentz spins are $\pm(h_J-1)$:

$$
s=\frac{8\pi}{\beta_{\rm SG}^2}-1=\lambda ,
$$ {#eq-nonlocal-spin}

the same $\lambda$ that appears in the sine-Gordon S-matrix (-@eq-sg-smatrix). For $\beta_{\rm SG}^2<8\pi$ the spin is positive and in general not an integer.

For a general $\hat g$ there are charges $Q_j$, $\bar Q_j$, one pair for each node $j=0,\dots,r$ of the affine Dynkin diagram, built from vertex operators of $\phi_L$ in the direction of the coroot $\vec\alpha_j^\vee$, together with the topological charges $\vec T$ [@bernard1991; @felder1992]. Since the vertex operators involve coroots, the relations they satisfy are those of the dual algebra. For simply-laced $\hat g$ every charge has spin $\frac{4\pi}{\beta^2}-1$ in the normalization of @sec-lie-algebraic-data; for $a_1^{(1)}$ this is (-@eq-nonlocal-spin), since $\beta_{\rm SG}^2=2\beta^2$.

## The coproduct and the algebra {#sec-qg-coproduct}

A non-local charge acting on a two-soliton state is not the sum of its actions on the two solitons. The charge density at a point $x$ involves the field to the left of $x$, through $\phi_L$. When the density passes the first soliton, it picks up a phase from the topological charge of that soliton. The result is a coproduct of the form

$$
\Delta(Q_j)=Q_j\otimes1+q^{T_j}\otimes Q_j ,
$$

where $T_j$ is the component of the topological charge along the corresponding coroot, and $q$ is the braiding phase of the chiral vertex operators. With this coproduct Bernard and LeClair find [@bernard1991]

$$
q=e^{-i\pi h_J}=e^{-8\pi^2i/\beta_{\rm SG}^2}=e^{-4\pi^2i/\beta^2},
$$ {#eq-q-physical}

which for sine-Gordon is $q=-e^{-i\pi\lambda}$. For a general $\hat g$, $q_j=q^{\vec\alpha_j^{\vee2}/2}$. This is the structure of @sec-hopf: the coproduct is not cocommutative, and the order of the solitons matters. It is the opposite of the coproduct (-@eq-coproduct), and with (-@eq-coproduct) the same charges give $q^{-1}$, the value of @sec-six-vertex. The sign of $q$ is not a convention: it changes the relative sign of the transmission and reflection amplitudes (@sec-six-vertex), and only (-@eq-q-physical) reproduces Zamolodchikov's S-matrix and passes the crossing test of @sec-crossing-sign. Computing the commutation relations of the charges and the topological charges gives the Drinfeld–Jimbo relations of @sec-uqghat for $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$ at zero centre, with the $Q_j$ as the $e_j$, the $\bar Q_j\,q^{-T_j}$ as the $f_j$ (up to a constant), and $q^{T_j}$ as the $k_j$, for the coproduct $\Delta(e_j)=e_j\otimes1+k_j\otimes e_j$, $\Delta(f_j)=f_j\otimes k_j^{-1}+1\otimes f_j$ [@bernard1991; @felder1992]. For sine-Gordon this is $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$: $(Q_+,\bar Q_-,T)$ give $(e_1,f_1,k_1)$ and $(Q_-,\bar Q_+,-T)$ give $(e_0,f_0,k_0)$.

**Why the dual algebra.** The vertex operators that define the charges are exponentials of $\phi_L$ in directions $\vec\alpha_j^\vee$, and their mutual braiding is governed by the inner products $\vec\alpha_i^\vee\cdot\vec\alpha_j^\vee$, which form the Cartan matrix of the dual root system (@sec-dynkin). For simply-laced and self-dual algebras the distinction disappears. For $c_n^{(1)}$, for example, the soliton symmetry is $U_q(d_{n+1}^{(2)})$, which is why Part VI needs R-matrices of twisted algebras.

## Lorentz spin and the gradation {#sec-qg-gradation}

The solitons of a multiplet form a representation of $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$ in which the charges act on one-soliton states of rapidity $\theta$. A Lorentz boost by $\vartheta$ multiplies a charge of spin $s$ by $e^{s\vartheta}$ and shifts the rapidity of the soliton. So the representation on solitons of rapidity $\theta$ is an evaluation representation $V(x)$ whose spectral parameter depends on $\theta$. If $e_j$ has spin $s_j$, it acts with a factor $e^{s_j\theta}=x^{s_j/2T}$, where $x=e^{2T\theta}$. Gradations that redistribute the spins among the generators are related by rapidity-dependent changes of basis (@sec-gradations), so only the total spin $\sum_jn_j^\vee s_j$ of the null root $\sum_jn_j^\vee\vec\alpha_j^\vee$ of $\hat g^\vee$ (normalized by $n_0^\vee=1$, since $x$ multiplies $e_0$ once) is fixed, and it determines $T$. The charge of node $j$ is built from $\exp(-i\frac{4\pi}\beta\vec\alpha_j^\vee\cdot\vec\phi_L)$, of weight $8\pi/(\beta^2\vec\alpha_j^2)$, so its spin is

$$
s_j=\frac{8\pi}{\beta^2\vec\alpha_j^2}-1 :
$$

$\frac{4\pi}{\beta^2}-1$ for long roots, $\frac{8\pi}{\beta^2}-1$ for roots of squared length 1, $\frac{12\pi}{\beta^2}-1$ for roots of squared length $\frac23$. With the normalization of @sec-amplitude-and-gradation,

$$
x(\theta)=e^{2T\theta},\qquad2T=\sum_jn_j^\vee s_j ,
$$

[@delius1995; @gmw1996]. For untwisted $\hat g$, $n_j^\vee=n_j\vec\alpha_j^2/2$ and the sum is exactly $2T=\frac{4\pi h}{\beta^2}-h^\vee$. For twisted $\hat g=X^{(k)}$, $n_j^\vee=k\,n_j\vec\alpha_j^2/2$, and the same formula holds with $\beta^2$ replaced by $\beta_{\rm lit}^2=\beta^2/k$ (@sec-conventions) and $h^\vee=\sum_jn_j^\vee$. For simply-laced $\hat g$, $2T=\sum_jn_j\big(\frac{4\pi}{\beta^2}-1\big)$. For sine-Gordon, $T=\lambda$.

Two checks show that this is right.

- **Crossing.** Crossing requires $x(i\pi)=x_c$, the crossing point of @sec-qg-crossing. For sine-Gordon in the homogeneous gradation, with the coproduct of @sec-qg-coproduct, $x_c=q^{-2}$ ($q^2$ for that of @sec-hopf), and $e^{2\pi i\lambda}=q^{-2}$ holds exactly for $q=-e^{-i\pi\lambda}$.
- **Breathers.** In the rapidity variable $t=T\theta/(i\pi)$ of @sec-amplitude-and-gradation, the sine-Gordon breather poles $\theta=i(\pi-n\xi)$ lie at $t=T-nT\xi/\pi=T-n$, because $T\xi=\pi$. These are the breather towers that Part VI uses for every algebra (@sec-breather-test).

## Consequences for the S-matrix {#sec-qg-consequences}

The non-local charges commute with the S-matrix. If the two-soliton states of multiplets $a$ and $b$ form a representation $V_a(x_1)\otimes V_b(x_2)$ that is irreducible for generic rapidities, Schur's lemma gives

$$
S_{ab}(\theta)=\Phi_{ab}(\theta)\,\check R_{ab}\big(x(\theta)\big),
$$

the form used throughout Part VI. The R-matrix is fixed by the quantum group, and the scalar factor $\Phi_{ab}$ by unitarity, crossing, the bootstrap and minimality. Several further consequences follow.

- **Multiplets.** The solitons of species $a$ form a finite-dimensional representation of $U_q(\hat g^\vee)$ whose weights are the topological charges. For $a_n^{(1)}$ these are the fundamental representations $\Lambda^a\mathbb C^{n+1}$. The classical solitons of @sec-topological-charges realize only some of these weights. This is the missing-charge problem (@sec-missing-charges).
- **Bound states and fusion.** Poles of $\check R$ project onto submodules (@sec-fusion), so bound-state multiplets are representations obtained by fusion, and the bootstrap is fusion of R-matrices.
- **Breathers.** Breathers are quantum-group singlets, so their scattering with solitons is a scalar times the identity, and among themselves they scatter diagonally. This is why they can be compared with the particle S-matrices of Part IV.
- **No unitarity for free.** For $\lvert q\rvert=1$ the invariant Hermitian forms on tensor products are indefinite, and the $*$-structure reverses tensor factors (@sec-qg-hermitian). The quantum group therefore does not make the S-matrix unitary. It makes it **Krein-unitary** (@sec-krein-unitarity), and whether it is unitary in the QFT sense depends on the basis (@sec-rsos).

What the symmetry does not fix is the scalar factor, and in particular the positions of its zeros modulo integers (@sec-integer-lifts). Those must be fixed by physics: the soliton masses, the breather–particle identification, and perturbation theory. Chapters [-@sec-sm-construction]–[-@sec-sm-f4] show how far this goes.

## Exercises {#sec-qg-symmetry-exercises}

::: {#exr-nonlocal-spin}
A density of conformal weights $(h,\bar h)$ has Lorentz spin $h-\bar h$, and $\int dx$ lowers the spin by one. Use this to show that $\int dx\,J_\pm$ has spin $h_J-1$, and check that $H_\pm$ must then have weights $(h_J-1,1)$ up to $O(m_0^2)$ corrections.
:::

::: {#exr-coproduct-q}
Show that $\Delta(Q)=Q\otimes1+q^{T}\otimes Q$ is coassociative, and compare with (-@eq-coproduct). Which generator of $U_q(sl_2)$ corresponds to $Q$, and with which convention for $K$?
:::

::: {#exr-sg-gradation}
For sine-Gordon, verify $2T=\frac{4\pi h}{\beta^2}-h^\vee=2\lambda$, and that the breather poles sit at $t=T-n$. Where in $t$ is the crossing point?
:::

::: {#exr-an-gradation}
For $a_n^{(1)}$, show that $2T=h\omega$ with $\omega=\frac{4\pi}{\beta^2}-1$, and that the fusing angle $u_{11}^2=2\pi/h$ corresponds to $t=\omega$.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-qg-symmetry-notes}

The non-local charges of sine-Gordon and their $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ algebra are due to Bernard and LeClair [-@bernard1991], and the extension to affine Toda theories to Felder and LeClair [-@felder1992]. Delius [-@delius1995] showed that the Lorentz spins of the charges fix the gradation, and that crossing, the bootstrap and braiding unitarity follow from the Hopf-algebra structure. Gandenberger, MacKay and Watts [@gmw1996] give the formula for $T$ used in Part VI. The quantum-group structure of affine Toda solitons is also studied by Hollowood [-@hollowood1993b] and Efthimiou [@efthimiou1993].
